text: Gemini lets you set standing instructions for what it should know about you and how you want it to respond, so you don't have to repeat the same preferences in every conversation. One important note before we start. Instructions for Gemini currently apply to personal Google accounts. If you're signed in with a work, school or supervised account, you won't see this option. Let's start with where to find them. On web, sign in to Gemini with your personal Google account, then go to settings and help select personal intelligence and open instructions for Gemini. Depending on your app version or location, you may see this personalization area called personal intelligence or personal context. I'll open personal intelligence and go to instructions for Gemini. Gemini gives me one main field for my instructions, so I'm going to organize everything using the three Cs. Context, Communication and Collaboration. I'll select the instruction field and enter my complete profile. For context, I lead strategy and operations and regularly use Gemini to prepare for meetings, evaluate business decisions, and communicate recommendations to senior stakeholders. For communication, lead with the main takeaway, keep responses concise, use straightforward business language, and use bullets when they make information easier to scan. And finally, for collaboration. Challenge my assumptions when appropriate. Surface important risks and trade-offs, flag uncertainty rather than guessing, and ask questions when missing information could materially change your recommendation. Once I select submit, my instructions are saved. And that's it. Gemini now has a starting profile for who I am, how I wanted to communicate, and how I wanted to collaborate with me, without me having to repeat those instructions in every conversation. If I ever want to temporarily stop using these instructions, I can turn them off using the toggle in the upper right corner. Now let's test it in a fresh conversation. I'll ask Gemini. I'm considering expanding into Singapore next year. Do you think this is a market worth exploring, and what would you want me to validate before committing resources? Now I'm not just looking at the content of Gemini's answer, I'm also looking for signs that my personalization is shaping the response. Does Gemini approach the question from the perspective of a senior leader? Does it get to the key takeaway quickly? Does it surface risks and trade-offs instead of simply agreeing with me? And is the answer structured in a way that's easy for me to use? Those are all signals that my instructions are having in effect. If something feels off, I can go back and refine them. For example, if Gemini consistently gives me more detail than I need, I could make my communication instruction more specific. Keep responses under 200 words unless I ask for more detail and use no more than five bullets. Instead of repeating that preference in every conversation, I can update my standing instructions and test again. Now a few things to keep in mind. First, your instructions follow your Google account across supported devices, so you don't need to recreate them on each device. Second, your account-wide instructions for Gemini don't automatically apply inside gems. Gemini Reusable Assistant, so add any relevant guidance directly to the gem when needed. And finally, don't use instructions as a way to make Gemini forget previously stored information. For that, use Gemini's activity and data controls. As you notice patterns in what works, or find yourself repeatedly correcting Gemini in the same way, update your instructions.
